note: Defines the metric-subjectivity spectrum (the x-axis of the 5.1 headline slope). The articulability_tier column is a PRIOR for design only - the measured x-value comes from recon-channel bits / codability census, never from this file. Do not run confirmatory passes until the user signs off the battery (gate G1).

outcome.prompt_name: Overall: should this paper be accepted?
outcome.role: distal aggregate reward (the target model's holistic judgment; never the real ICLR decision in v1)

metrics.name: Experiments support the claims
metrics.definition: The experimental evidence presented is sufficient to support the paper's stated claims.

metrics.name: Has adequate baselines
metrics.definition: Comparisons include the appropriate and reasonably strong baseline methods.

metrics.name: Reproducible from the text
metrics.definition: A competent reader could re-implement the method and reproduce the main results from the paper alone.

metrics.name: Novel contribution
metrics.definition: The paper contributes something genuinely new relative to prior work.

metrics.name: Significant contribution
metrics.definition: The results matter - they change what the field knows or can do.

metrics.name: Clearly written
metrics.definition: The paper is well organized and its arguments are easy to follow.

metrics.name: Good taste in problem selection
metrics.definition: The authors chose a good problem.

design_notes: Low-tier metric definitions are DELIBERATELY thin (near name-only): their whole point is that the construct is preference-defined, so a rich definition would beg the question.
Reliability precondition: every metric needs >=2 reps x >=2 prompt forms of target judgments for test-retest noise ceilings BEFORE the slope is interpretable (audit F3).
Residualization set = the high-tier metrics; the residual of holistic_accept on them is the training signal for the reward channel (5.1).
